newsitem.title: USA: Bergen Brunswig, IVAX in option deal.
newsitem.headline: Bergen Brunswig, IVAX in option deal.

text.p: Bergen Brunswig Corp said Thursday that IVAX Corp has granted it an option to buy up to 30.18 million shares of IVAX at $12.375 a share.
Bergen Brunswig, which announced on November 11 it agreed to buy the generic drug maker in a $1.6 billion deal, disclosed the option in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The Orange, Calif.,-based drug wholesaler said it also entered into a voting agreement with Dr. Philip Frost, chairman and chief executive of IVAX, and a partnership controllled by Frost.
Under the agreement, Frost and the partnership will vote their 12.5 percent stake, or about 15.1 million common shares, in favor of the merger deal and against any competing transaction.
The stock option and the voting agreement gives Bergen Brunswig the equivalent of a 29.9 percent stake, or 45.3 million shares, according to the filing.
As an inducement for IVAX to enter into the merger deal, Bergen Brunswig also granted the company a reciprocal option in which IVAX may buy up to 9,953,076 Bergen Brunswig shares for $27.625.
Bergen Brunswig shares closed down 5/8 at 27-1/4, while IVAX stock dropped 1/8 at 11-1/4.
Both options are exercisable under certain conditions related to the merger agreement.
